title: Reactogenicity and safety of the human rotavirus vaccine, Rotarix™ in The Philippines, Sri Lanka, and India: a post-marketing surveillance study.
ehr_evidence: Baseline demographic data was reported on the case report form by the investigators at the time of enrolment/first visit, and adverse events were recorded on diary cards after each vaccine dose; data were collected via study case report forms/eCRF, not pre-existing electronic health records.
summary: Three open, single-group, uncontrolled post-marketing surveillance studies evaluated the reactogenicity and safety of two doses of the Rotarix rotavirus vaccine administered to healthy infants (aged ≥6 weeks) in The Philippines, Sri Lanka, and India.
key_findings: At least one Grade 2/3 solicited adverse event (fever, vomiting, or diarrhea) was reported in 14.7% (95% CI: 12.9–16.7) of infants in The Philippines, 14.9% (95% CI: 12.0–18.3) in Sri Lanka, and 12.7% (95% CI: 9.3–16.7) in India.

Irritability was the most frequently reported solicited AE in The Philippines (32.2% post-Dose-1; 23.5% post-Dose-2) and India (23.0% post-Dose-1; 13.2% post-Dose-2), and fever in Sri Lanka (18.0% post-Dose-1; 20.2% post-Dose-2).
Unsolicited AEs were recorded in 24.5% (95% CI: 22.3–26.8) of infants in The Philippines, 4.8% (95% CI: 3.1–7.0) in Sri Lanka, and 6.9% (95% CI: 4.4–10.2) in India.

Forty-one SAEs occurred in 33 infants in The Philippines of which six in four infants were assessed as causally related to vaccination; one vaccine-unrelated SAE occurred in Sri Lanka; no SAEs were reported in India.

One infant in The Philippines developed life-threatening intussusception 1 day after the first dose, judged possibly related to the vaccine but confounded by infectious diarrhea; the infant was lost to follow-up.
Two doses of Rotarix administered according to local prescribing information had no new safety concerns and were well tolerated in all three countries.
captured_features: Solicited adverse events (fever, vomiting, diarrhea, irritability, cough/runny nose, loss of appetite) with grade 2/3 intensity
Serious adverse events and causal relationship to vaccination
study_design: Post-marketing surveillance, open-label, single-group, uncontrolled, multi-center observational studies
population: Healthy infants aged at least 6 weeks at first dose of Rotarix in The Philippines (n=1494 enrolled), Sri Lanka (n=522), and India (n=332)
limitations: Small sample size limited the ability to identify rare adverse events
Open, single-group, uncontrolled design with no randomization
Passive adverse event reporting and difficulties in follow-up led to underreporting of AEs and SAEs
Different infant exclusion criteria across the three countries
The single intussusception case was lost to follow-up, so the duration of the SAE could not be determined
